title: Form 8822 Guide: Deceased Person's IRS Address Update (October 2026)
summary: A step-by-step look at Form 8822 for executors managing a deceased person's IRS mailing address in October 2026.
body_markdown:
After a death, the IRS sends mail about the person's individual taxes to the last address it has on file. Form 8822 changes that mailing address so notices reach the executor, which is especially important if the former home is being sold or emptied. The IRS also requires proof of the executor's authority, and an estate's separate tax account is updated with Form 8822-B. This guide explains key points for executors and families to be aware of, including: what Form 8822 does, how it differs from Form 8822-B, which documents prove authority, what information the form needs, how it is submitted, and more.


**Key Takeaways**


- Form 8822 updates personal IRS mailing records; Form 8822-B updates an estate's EIN record.
- Form 8822 alone does not prove executor authority. Supporting documents are required.
- Forms 8822 and 8822-B cannot be filed online. Both are normally printed, signed, and mailed.
- IRS mailing updates can take roughly 4 to 6 weeks. Access to the former mailbox may be needed.
- Elayne tracks pending IRS notifications.


## What Form 8822 Does in an Estate Context


Form 8822 updates where the IRS sends mail for individual, gift, estate, or generation-skipping transfer tax records. For an executor, it helps redirect tax correspondence tied to the person who died, and works alongside the broader process to[notify the IRS of a death](https://www.elayne.com/resources/how-to-notify-the-irs-of-a-death-reporting-and-final-tax-responsibilities) . The[IRS Form 8822 PDF](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8822.pdf) identifies the tax records covered.


If the deceased person’s former home is being emptied, sold, or transferred, refund checks and tax notices could arrive where no one regularly collects mail. Updating the mailing information helps the person handling these tax matters receive correspondence during estate settlement.

## Form 8822 vs. Form 8822-B: Which One Applies to the Estate


The form depends on which IRS record needs updating. An estate may need separate updates for personal and entity records.


Record being updated Form


Deceased person’s individual mailing information IRS Form 8822


Business or entity with an EIN, including an estate’s income tax account[IRS Form 8822-B](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8822-b)


Updating personal records does not update business records, so both forms may be needed.


## Why the Executor Must Document Authority With the IRS First


The IRS requires proof of authority before acting on requests involving a deceased person’s records. This helps protect the deceased person’s confidential tax information from unauthorized access. That proof accompanies or precedes the mailing-change request.


[Form 56 notifies the IRS](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-56) of "a fiduciary relationship under section 6903."


Under the[IRS proof requirements](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/request-deceased-persons-information) , requests for the deceased person’s information include a death certificate copy and either court-approved[Letters Testamentary](https://www.elayne.com/resources/what-are-letters-testamentary-the-document-every-executor-needs-and-how-to-get-it) or Form 56.


Form 8822 alone does not prove an executor’s authority. Missing supporting documents can delay the request.


## What Information Is Required to Complete Form 8822 for a Deceased Person


The Form 8822 field layout separates individual income tax records from estate tax records:


- For individual income tax records, the deceased person’s name and Social Security number go in the main identification fields.
- The estate and generation-skipping transfer tax checkbox has separate fields for the decedent’s name and Social Security number.
- The old mailing location is the last one the IRS has on file for that taxpayer.
- The new mailing location is where future correspondence should go, typically the executor’s home or the estate’s designated mailing location, one of several items in the broader set of[executor of estate paperwork](https://www.elayne.com/resources/executor-of-estate-paperwork) to track.


## Can Form 8822 Be Filed Online? Submission Methods Explained


Neither Form 8822 nor Form 8822-B can be filed online. Fillable PDFs can be completed on a computer, but both forms ordinarily must be printed, signed, and mailed.


The mailing destination depends on the former mailing location’s state and filing context. Each form’s IRS instructions list the destination. Fax is an option for a responsible-party change only when the IRS permits it for that case.


IRS mailing updates can take approximately 4 to 6 weeks. Executors may need continued access to mail at the former location during processing.


## What Mailing Location to List


The receiving location listed on Form 8822 should stay accessible throughout settlement, with someone responsible for opening IRS mail and responding. Some points to consider:


- An executor’s home offers direct access.
- An attorney’s office may work if the attorney agrees to receive correspondence and promptly share it with the executor.
- A P.O. box keeps estate mail separate from household mail. However, someone needs to collect it regularly.


This choice concerns the deceased person’s tax records. An estate’s separate EIN mailing record, created when the executor first[gets an EIN for the estate](https://www.elayne.com/resources/how-to-get-ein-number-for-estate-account) , is updated through Form 8822-B. The two records are handled separately.


## Why This Step Matters for SECURE Act 2.0 and Inherited Retirement Accounts


[Inherited retirement account taxes](https://www.elayne.com/resources/executor-inherited-ira-tax-rules) can involve annual withdrawals, called required minimum distributions (RMDs), depending on the beneficiary and account.


- In 2026, certain beneficiaries must take annual withdrawals during the 10-year distribution period under the[inherited IRA distribution rules](https://www.elayne.com/resources/inherited-ira-distribution-rules) .
- Under SECURE Act 2.0, a missed RMD can trigger a[25% excise tax](https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/retirement-plan-and-ira-required-minimum-distributions-faqs) on the amount not withdrawn, with possible reductions or waivers.


## Where Form 8822 Fits in the Broader Estate Settlement Process


Form 8822 belongs early in estate organization and notification work, once the executor’s authority is documented. It can be prepared alongside related IRS notifications.


Documenting authority and updating IRS records supports later requests for transcripts, refund follow-up, responses to correspondence, and eventually an[estate tax closing letter](https://www.elayne.com/resources/how-to-request-an-estate-tax-closing-letter-from-the-irs) from the IRS.


The broader tax checklist may include:


- Final Form 1040 for the deceased person’s individual income taxes.
- [Form 1041](https://www.elayne.com/resources/form-1041-estate-tax-return) for estate income taxes, when required.
- Form 706 for estate taxes, if applicable.


These filings serve separate purposes. The mailing update helps route IRS correspondence to the person managing them.

## FAQ


### What’s a practical way to track Form 8822 with Elayne when multiple relatives are helping?


A shared record with one named person responsible for submission helps prevent duplicate filings. In Elayne, authorized users can keep the signed copy, mailing date, delivery proof, and pending follow-up together; the family or the professional supporting them remains responsible for submitting the form.


### How does an executor document that Form 8822 was mailed to the IRS?


A retained copy of the signed form, supporting documents, and a mailing receipt helps create a record of what was sent and when. Certified mail or another trackable mailing method can help provide delivery evidence.


### Does the IRS charge a fee to file Form 8822?


No. The IRS does not charge a fee to file Form 8822 or Form 8822-B, and both forms are free to download from IRS.gov. The only costs involved are postage and any trackable mailing service chosen.


### Is there a deadline to file Form 8822 after someone dies?


The 60-day deadline applies to responsible-party changes reported on Form 8822-B. For a deceased person’s individual mailing record, the IRS continues sending mail to the last mailing location on file until the update is processed. For that reason, the update is commonly prepared early in estate settlement.


### Who signs Form 8822 for a deceased person?


The Form 8822 instructions explain who signs when a taxpayer has died. An executor or other personal representative typically signs, and supporting documents such as Letters Testamentary or Form 56 show that authority to the IRS.


### Does U.S. Postal Service mail forwarding replace Form 8822?


No. Postal forwarding redirects mail at the post office, while Form 8822 changes the mailing location the IRS has on record. The two are separate systems. The Postal Service offers a change-of-mailing-location option for executors and other authorized representatives, but it does not update IRS records.


### Does Form 8822 also update state tax agency records?


No. Form 8822 changes federal IRS records only. State tax agencies keep their own mailing records and have their own procedures for updating them.


### Does an executor need an EIN before filing Form 8822 for the deceased person?


No. Form 8822 for the deceased person’s individual records uses that person’s Social Security number. An EIN is used for the estate’s separate tax account, such as for filing Form 1041, and that mailing record is updated with Form 8822-B.


### Where is a refund check for a deceased person mailed?


A refund check is generally mailed to the mailing location shown on the return that claims it.[Form 1310](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-1310) is used when someone other than a surviving spouse on a joint return or a court-appointed representative is claiming the refund. A court-appointed representative filing an original return attaches a copy of the court document showing the appointment.
